text:
### Observed differences

- Six activities lost their mandatory status. Earlier, A28, A30, A31, A32, A33 and A34 each appeared exactly once in every trace (participation 100 in 100). In the later window, A28, A30 and A31 each appear in about 47 in 100 traces (93 of 200) and A32, A33 and A34 in about 56 in 100 (111 of 200); none of them occurs more than once per trace in either window. A25 and A26 continue to appear in every trace in both windows. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, POS001, POS002]
- A25's hand-over widened. Earlier, its outgoing flow went only to A28 (about 34 in 100), A30 (about 37) and A31 (about 30). In the later window those shares fell to about 15, 18 and 14 in 100, while A32 (about 16), A33 (about 18) and A34 (about 20) became direct successors of A25. [DIR001]
- The first trio now often hands over straight to A26. Earlier, A28, A30 and A31 never led to A26; in the later window roughly 34, 35 and 26 in 100 of their outgoing transitions go directly to A26, while their transitions into A32, A33 and A34 fell to about 1 in 100 each. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]
- Step distances shrank where the new direct edges appear. A32, A33 and A34 followed A25 four to five steps later in essentially all earlier observations; in the later window they follow within one to three steps in about 96–99 in 100 of the observed pairs. A26 likewise followed A28, A30 and A31 at four to five steps before, and now follows within one to three steps. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG008, LAG011]
- Event positions moved consistently with this: A25's mean position shifted slightly later (0.62 to 0.67 of the trace) and A26's slightly earlier (0.83 to 0.81), the first trio moved later (about 0.68 to 0.74) and the second trio earlier (about 0.77 to 0.74), so the two groups now sit at nearly the same relative position. These are event positions, not clock times. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008]
- The sequencing between the two trios after the change is weakly documented: ordered sequences such as A28→A32 or A30→A33, observed in essentially every earlier trace, appear in only about 4 later traces each, so proportions based on them are unreliable. [LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG009, LAG010, LAG012, LAG013]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the segment between A25 and A26 became partially optional and is often bypassed: A28, A30 and A31, formerly executed once in every case, now run in about 47 in 100 cases, and A32, A33 and A34 in about 56 in 100; A25 now feeds directly into all six activities instead of only the first three; and A28, A30 and A31 frequently hand over directly to A26, so the second trio is skipped in a large share of cases. [OCC001, OCC004, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, LAG001, LAG004]

The screening context supports going beyond chance: 31 of 100 tested control-flow units qualified against about 0.5 expected if nothing had changed, and every item's difference exceeds those seen in about 99.5 in 100 random re-splits of the pooled traces. The occurrence, routing and distance items all describe one coherent picture; the participation drops rest on 200 versus 93–111 supporting traces, the new edges are read directly from the routing profiles, and the distance collapse from four–five steps to one–three steps matches those edges rather than resting on position alone. Several items describe the same traces, so they are not independent confirmations. [OCC001, OCC006, DIR001, DIR002, LAG001, LAG008]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish whether each of the six activities became independently optional or whether roughly half of the cases now run a shortened variant that skips the block as a whole; the post-change ordering among the six activities rests on about 4 observations per pair; and the position shifts are event positions, not clock-time moves. [LAG005, LAG012, POS003]
